subject: maths
title: Perimeter and area

slides.heading: Perimeter and area — two different things that easy to mix up
slides.body: Perimeter is the total distance around the outside of a shape — you add up every side length. Area is the amount of flat space inside a shape — it's always measured in square units (cm², m², etc.). The two are completely different measurements, but exam questions often give you one and ask for the other, so make sure you read what's actually being asked.
slides.note: Maximum 3 sentences. Plain English. No AQA references. What is this and why does it matter.

slides.heading: Area formulae for 2D shapes
slides.formula: Rectangle: A = l × w  |  Triangle: A = ½ × b × h  |  Parallelogram: A = b × h  |  Trapezium: A = ½(a + b) × h  |  Circle: A = πr²
slides.formulaExplained: For a rectangle, multiply length by width. For a triangle, the height must be perpendicular to the base (the vertical height, not the slant side). A parallelogram uses the same formula as a rectangle — base × perpendicular height, not the slant side. For a trapezium, a and b are the two parallel sides and h is the perpendicular distance between them; halve the sum of the parallel sides and multiply by height. Circle area uses the radius squared multiplied by π.
slides.whenToUse: Any question asking for the area of a 2D shape. Always check units — if lengths are in cm, area is in cm². Compound shapes: split into simpler shapes, find each area separately, then add (or subtract for cut-outs).
slides.note: Show formula in standard notation. Explain each variable. State when this formula applies.

slides.heading: Let's work through one
slides.question: A trapezium has parallel sides of 9 cm and 5 cm, and a perpendicular height of 6 cm. Find its area.

steps.instruction: Write the trapezium area formula. Identify a, b and h.
steps.working: A = ½(a + b) × h. Here a = 9, b = 5, h = 6.

steps.instruction: Multiply by ½ and then by h.

slides.conclusion: The area of the trapezium is 42 cm².
slides.note: Numbers must differ from any question in the question bank for this subtopic.

slides.heading: Watch out for this

mistakes.mistake: Using the slant height instead of the perpendicular height in the triangle or trapezium formula.
mistakes.correction: The height h must be at right angles to the base. If the diagram shows a slant side but not a vertical height, look for a small right-angle symbol or use Pythagoras to find the perpendicular height.

mistakes.mistake: Forgetting to halve in the triangle formula — writing A = b × h instead of A = ½ × b × h.
mistakes.correction: A triangle is exactly half a parallelogram with the same base and height. Always include the ½. Writing ½bh and then dividing by 2 again is a common double-error — do one or the other.

mistakes.mistake: Giving area in linear units (e.g. cm) instead of square units (cm²).
mistakes.correction: Area is always in square units. Write cm², m² or mm² — never just cm. If the question uses mixed units (some sides in cm, some in mm), convert everything to the same unit first.

slides.note: Minimum 2, maximum 3 mistakes. Specific not generic.

keyFacts.fact: Area of a trapezium = ½(a + b) × h, where a and b are the parallel sides and h is the perpendicular height.
keyFacts.examTip: This formula is given on the formula sheet — but you must correctly identify which sides are parallel and which measurement is the perpendicular height.

keyFacts.fact: Area of a triangle = ½ × base × perpendicular height. The height must be at 90° to the base.
keyFacts.examTip: In a non-right-angled triangle the height may be shown as a dashed line inside or outside the triangle — always measure to that dashed line, not to a slant edge.

keyFacts.fact: For compound shapes, split into rectangles and triangles, calculate each area separately, then add or subtract.
keyFacts.examTip: Draw the split lines clearly on the diagram and label each part with its dimensions — this avoids using the wrong measurements in each sub-calculation.

note: keyFacts: 2-4 entries. Exam-precise language. These are what Mabel writes into her notes.
